sweaty at work, an electric bicycle can give you that last little push—metaphorically and literally. Also, they’re really fun. I’ve never met anyone who has tried an electric bicycle and <em>not</em> wanted one; in the Netherlands, electric bicycles currently <a data-offer-url="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/01/bike-country-n0-1-dutch-electric-record-numbers-e-bikes-netherlands" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/01/bike-country-n0-1-dutch-electric-record-numbers-e-bikes-netherlands&quot;}" href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/01/bike-country-n0-1-dutch-electric-record-numbers-e-bikes-netherlands" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">outsell regular bicycles</a>. However, that four-figure price tag induces sticker shock. BaseText-eqOrNE UnifiedProductCardDescriptionWrapper-dyAmCu deqABF fxYvgV bLswap"><div><p>Enough friends have asked me to help them assemble their new ebike that I now recommend that everyone go to a shop. Going to a shop in person means you can try a bunch of bikes to find out what style you like and get sized properly. Shops usually include free assembly and a service program for 30 days or a year, so you don&#x27;t have to tinker in your driveway or garage. If you&#x27;re the kind of person who would pay an extra $250 for assembly from a company like Velofix, then going to a shop is worth it.</p><p>We&#x27;ve had great experiences with Cannondale&#x27;s Adventure Neo line (<a href="https://www.wired.com/review/cannondale-adventure-neo-3-eq/">8/10, WIRED Recommends</a>). With the latest Adventure Neo Allroad, Cannondale has switched out some of the components to make the bike more accessible. It has a 250-watt Bafang motor with a Bafang sensor and a thumb throttle, which makes it a <a href="https://www.wired.com/story/guide-to-ebike-classes/">class 2 ebike</a>, even though it tops out at 20 mph assist. It&#x27;s essentially a Rad Power Bike (see below) you can have assembled and tuned for you in a shop, but it&#x27;s versatile and nimble on both roads, trails, and gravel, and small enough to fit my 5&#x27;2&quot; height. I rode this for over a week on roads and dirt and gravel paths near my house. The step-through frame and small, fat tires make it easy for a kid to hop on while a parent holds the bike steady. It&#x27;s a little difficult to lock up at the thicker part of the frame, but the bike&#x27;s design includes thinner tubes that will work.</p></div></div><div class="UnifiedProductCardReviewSection-ekgYes cJDFYa"></div></div></div></div></div></li></ul></div></div></div></div></div><div class="LazyChunk-kMbfxl kVoYsH"><div data-testid="RowWrapper" class="BaseWrap-sc-gzmcOU RowWrapper-EQDhp deqABF fWZsjA GalleryPageChunkRow-eInvyO jdunEg"><div class="GridWrapper-cFSKbf kfCuhH grid grid-margins grid-items-2 grid-layout--adrail narrow" data-journey-hook="grid-wrapper"><div class="GridItem-beYvyV kCPYUp grid--item grid-layout__content"><div class=""><ul class="GalleryPageSlides-hsMHHj cLfJLB"><li class="gallery__slides__slide" id="6556a446d28860eac8fe8832"><div><div class="UnifiedProductCardBody-hIYvDT cYxZHF product-embed impressionTracking" data-item="{&quot;ctaAnalyticsName&quot;:&quot;buy-button-click&quot;,&quot;bookmarkMeta&quot;:{&quot;slug&quot;:&quot;gallery/best-cheap-electric-bikes&quot;,&quot;title&quot;:&quot;The Best Cheap Electric Bikes Under $2,000&quot;},&quot;brand&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;GoTrax&quot;},&quot;contentType&quot;:&quot;product&quot;,&quot;ctaHref&quot;:null,&quot;dangerousCredit&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;dangerousHed&quot;:&quot;Best Folding Bike&quot;,&quot;dek&quot;:[&quot;div&quot;,[&quot;p&quot;,&quot;I&#x27;ve had a hit-or-miss track record testing &quot;,[&quot;a&quot;,{&quot;href&quot;:&quot;https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-electric-scooters/&quot;,&quot;isExternal&quot;:false},&quot;GoTrax&#x27;s electric kick scooters&quot;],&quot;, but I&#x27;m pretty happy with its F2 foldable electric bike. But older adults might require a bike with a step-through frame or other accommodations to help them keep it from tipping over.</p><p>The solution is an electric tricycle, and this <a href="https://www.wired.com/story/guide-to-ebike-classes/">class 2 trike</a> from SixThreeZero fits the bill. It has a range of up to 60 miles, and there&#x27;s even a rear basket where your elderly loved one can put their small dog or a basket of library books. BaseText-eqOrNE UnifiedProductCardDescriptionWrapper-dyAmCu deqABF fxYvgV bLswap"><div><p>Ebikes come and ebikes go, but the one bike that I always want to have on hand is <a href="https://www.wired.com/story/jackrabbit-xg-rave/">a JackRabbit</a>. You might call it a microbike. This is the most useful electric bike I have tested for what city planners call trip-chaining, or putting multiple trips together. This is a bike that you can easily throw into a trunk and zip off to the grocery store while your kids are at the park, or if you want to drop off your car at Les Schwab and zip home for two to three hours.</p><p>The <a data-offer-url="https://jackrabbit.bike/products/jackrabbit?variant=41475026583720" class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://cna.st/affiliate-&quot;}" href="https://cna.st/affiliate-" rel="sponsored" target="_blank">cheaper OG rings in at $1,000</a>, but the new XG has a slightly longer frame, a 500-watt motor, and two swappable battery slots. More power and more range make it much more useful than the original JackRabbit, even if it is a little bigger. (I do have to admit that it was funny forcing my much larger spouse to ride up and down the street on a quarter-sized electric bike.) I enjoy puttering around my neighborhood and startling my neighbors when I zip around a corner on something that looks like what their child should be riding. Certification?</h3></div></div><div class="UnifiedProductCardOfferContainer-dSdPtc bhGeQJ"></div></div></div></div><div class="UnifiedLandscapeProductCardDescDetails-yYdHD ivCCL"><div class="BaseWrap-sc-gzmcOU BaseText-eqOrNE UnifiedProductCardDescriptionWrapper-dyAmCu deqABF fxYvgV bLswap"><div><p>Even cheap ebikes are vehicles, not toys. In our years of testing electric bikes, we&#x27;ve had components snap on us at 20 miles per hour; we&#x27;ve had pedals break off, kicked fenders as we rode, and even had <a data-offer-url="https://www.dubizzle.com/blog/cars/arcing-in-automobiles/#:~:text=Electric%20arcing%20in%20automobiles%20usually,worn%2Dout%20and%20broken%20wires." class="external-link" data-event-click="{&quot;element&quot;:&quot;ExternalLink&quot;,&quot;outgoingURL&quot;:&quot;https://www.dubizzle.com/blog/cars/arcing-in-automobiles/#:~:text=Electric%20arcing%20in%20automobiles%20usually,worn%2Dout%20and%20broken%20wires.&quot;}" href="https://www.dubizzle.com/blog/cars/arcing-in-automobiles/#:~:text=Electric%20arcing%20in%20automobiles%20usually,worn%2Dout%20and%20broken%20wires." rel="nofollow" target="_blank">drive trains arc on us</a> as we were assembling them. It&#x27;s important that we recommend a safe bike.</p><p>The most important factor we look for as we test ebikes is UL certification. As ebikes have boomed in popularity, so have the number of deadly fires from charging poorly regulated <a href="https://apnews.com/article/ebike-fires-lithium-ion-batteries-b5ab9acf9ca317a1b5b917097ac5210d">lithium-ion batteries</a>. Starting on September 16, 2023, New York City requires that all battery-operated mobility devices sold, rented, or leased in New York City be certified by an accredited testing laboratory <a href="https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/news/044-23/city-reminds-retailers-consumers-only-purchase-certified-lithium-ion-batteries-mobility">to comply</a> with Underwriters Laboratories (UL) safety standards.</p><p>You don&#x27;t have to let safety considerations deter you from buying a cheap ebike, but we would urge you to consider a few basic safety rules. As a general rule of thumb, treat your bike like you would any other giant battery. Do not leave it charging overnight. Do not use a third-party charger. If it gets smashed, starts leaking, or looks weird, leave it alone and call the fire department. And as always, do not let your children ride it or <a href="https://www.wired.com/story/do-not-put-kids-on-electric-bikes/">play with it unattended</a>.</p></div></div><div
